"DM: when I get out, can I still hear the bell in town, and is Brannoc Vell's watch answering it yet?"

input.add_to_description: Harbour watch horn heard answering the shrine bell from the Grand Quay on Day 2 about 7:45 PM; the watch is mustering but Deputy Thack stands at the foot of the hill road.

entries.text:
The gallery is a cold, ankle-deep crawl, low enough that your horns scrape the stone. Your darkvision shows you the way as the lamp's gold fades behind you. The tunnel climbs and bends, and the drip of water grows louder until the stone opens into the Water-Stair's landing, under the carved lantern arch. You come out just ahead of Odalie, who is leaning on the wall there with her breath rasping. She pats your wrist without a word and keeps moving.

At the river-door the night air hits your face, and the sounds of the town come with it. The shrine bell has stopped. Someone stilled it, and the silence on the hill is worse than the ringing. But from down by the water, thin and clear, a harbour horn is sounding, three long notes and a pause, again and again. Lanterns are bobbing along the Grand Quay, and a line of them is starting up the hill road. Brannoc Vell's watch is answering, though at the foot of the road, a knot of torches has stopped and is arguing. That will be Sorrel Thack.

Two things on your sheet puzzle me, so I'll flag them rather than hide them. It now shows you at level 2 with 425 XP, a total I can't match to what I tracked. It lists a "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin" in your pack, and I have no record of that item or person, so I won't pretend I know its story. Your rapier is also missing from the item list. You may want to tell me what you remember of these.

Time is the same as before: it's a quarter to eight at night, Ashgrove is at the shrine and you hold the key. What does Vesper do?

entries.text:
The Keepers' gallery slopes up through the hill, ankle-deep in cold water, with a ceiling low enough that you stoop. Behind you the lamp's gold dwindles to a coin, then a spark, then is gone, and your darkvision paints the wet walls silver-grey. Twice you pass carved lanterns with names under them. You don't stop to read them.

It's about ten minutes before the tunnel opens onto the Water-Stair, at the landing under the carved lantern arch. You can hear the bell here, but only faintly. It's no longer ringing in strokes. It tolls slow and tired, one note every few breaths, the way a swinging bell dies down by itself. Nobody is hauling it now.

Farther off, from the town side, you catch something new: the clatter of a watchman's rattle, then another answering it from the direction of the Grand Quay, and the thin shout of a man calling names. Lanterns are moving in the lanes below the hill. There are not many, perhaps five or six, and they are bunching at the foot of the hill road, where Sorrel Thack and his two men were posted. Voices are arguing there. You can't make out the words, only the tone of one man refusing to be told "for order" any longer.

Far above, muffled by stone, Ashgrove's men are pounding on the undercroft door. The captain's pleasant voice carries once, faintly: "Harl, bring the other barge crews up the hill."

The Water-Stair drops away below you toward the net-sheds and Mags's house, where Odalie and Tamsin should be. The Reeve's lanterns are gathering at the other side of the hill. There's no spell left in you, and Disguise Self still holds for about three quarters of an hour.

entries.text:
The gallery is a cold, ankle-deep crawl, and the gold of the lamp shrinks behind you to a coin and then to nothing. Your darkvision does the rest. The roof presses low enough that you stoop, and the carved lanterns on the walls give way to bare, weeping stone. The sound of the water carries the dull thump of the ram for a while, and then the hill swallows it.

Ten minutes of climbing brings you out at the landing under the carved lantern arch, where the Water-Stair joins the tunnel. The bell is silent. Someone up top stopped it, or cut the rope. But the cold air coming up from the river brings other sounds instead. Far down in the lower town a watch-horn is blowing the short, repeated call that means a summons. Dogs are barking, shutters are banging, and a ragged crowd is shouting somewhere near the foot of the hill road. Over it all comes one flat voice, loud and unhurried, shouting for the Harbour Reeve's watch to form up. It doesn't sound like Sorrel Thack's.

You can't tell yet who has answered the bell, the Reeve or only the curious. There's no sign of Odalie on the stair, and no sign of anyone behind you. Below, the net-sheds and Mags's lamp-lit window wait. The river is a black ribbon past them, and Corvin's *Plump Heron* is probably still tied at Tanner's Stair, if he kept his word about the second bell.

You have the key, Thack's pay-chit and a locked door between Ashgrove and the wyrm. Your spell slots are spent, and the Disguise Self still has about forty-five minutes on it.

line: Vesper turns her head on the pillow and manages a cracked smile, her tail finally allowed to twitch where everyone can see. "Sister, you can have the bowl back first, it was always yours, and then I want to hear every word Thack is singing about where Ashgrove's barges are bound." She tries to sit up and thinks better of it. "DM: how many hit points will I have after a long rest, and did Ysolt Pike come through the fight all right?"

input.description: Lean, squinting harbour-warden crossbow of Brannoc Vell's watch. Fought beside Vesper in the shrine-yard melee, received a Bardic Inspiration die from her, and survived with a bolt-graze on her shoulder.

entries.text: notebook: created an entry for Ysolt Pike

Odalie takes the bowl in both hands and doesn't answer, but her thumb moves once over the rim, and that is answer enough. "It was never the bowl, child," she says at last, and sets it back on your blanket. "Keep it until you have someplace to put it."

Ysolt Pike came through, and she's the first thing Odalie tells you. A raider's bolt grazed her shoulder, and she was back behind her fish-cart before the line broke. She has sworn, to anyone who'll listen, that the horned girl owes her a drink and a better shot. Brannoc Vell took a cut on his forearm and lost a boathook. Two of the watch are badly hurt, and none of them died. Thack is still singing. So far he's named a barge-master called Garrow Quill, a sluice-keeper somewhere south at the Greywater Weirs, and "the third night and the moon, always the moon."

As for your hit points, a long rest restores you to your full 15 and gives you back all three of your 1st-level slots. Half your spent hit dice come back too, and so do your Bardic Inspiration uses. It's about nine at night. If you sleep here until morning, you'll start the next day whole.

One thing needs fixing, and I'd rather say so than hide it. Your sheet shows a brass lantern key and half of a "sluice-pin" marked Garrow Quill's, but no rapier. I narrated Ashgrove taking the satchel and the key, and I never gave you either of those other things. It's possible the sheet has gone ahead of the story. Which do you want to have happened? Did Ashgrove take a copy or a false key, with the real one slipped to you in the scuffle, or did Garrow's pin-half come off a raider? And is the rapier gone, or lying somewhere in the yard? I'll set the story to match what you choose.

Odalie's hand tightens on your wrist. "Keep the bowl a little longer. Then give it back when you're ready, and not before I've scolded you properly." Her mouth wobbles, and she doesn't scold you yet.

Rules answers first. A long rest returns you to your full hit point maximum, which is 15, and restores your spell slots (all 3) and your Bardic Inspiration. You're at 13 of 15 now, so you're mostly there already. A night's sleep in Mags's back room does the rest.

Ysolt Pike came through it. She took a cut across the scalp and a cracked rib, and she's loud about both. Mags says she's drinking the Reeve's brandy by the shrine gate and telling anyone who'll listen that "the horned girl's bardic blessing gave me the shakes, and I still hit three of them."

One correction from me, because your sheet is the record and I narrated it wrong. The brass lantern key is still with you. Odalie found it clenched in your fist when they carried you in. Your sheet also lists "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin", and I have no record of it in play. Tell me where you got it and what it is, and I'll fit it into the story. Your rapier is also missing from the sheet. I'd say Odalie has it, propped by the door.

Thack in the lockup is singing about the barges. Which of those threads do you pull first?

Odalie presses the bowl back into your hands without a word, closes your fingers over it, and says only, "Later. When you've earned the right to be embarrassed about it."

The truth is that Ashgrove took the satchel and found it empty of the key. Mags found the key clenched in your fist when they carried you in, so you did hold on to it. Ashgrove has the vial's empty stopper and a letter, and a very bad mood.

line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

She keeps her tail tucked and her eyes on the cabin door while she signals Ysolt with two slow fingers down by her hip: *wait.* "Mind if I bring my own cup? I'd like to hear what a woman with half the words offers for the other half."

entries.text:
The sentry's crossbow follows you as you step up onto the barrels, light as a cat. Ashgrove watches you drop the disguise with the interest of a woman watching a card trick she has already seen. Her eyes flick once to the hand you keep low at your hip, and she lets it pass.

"Cup. Yes, of course." She stands aside from the cabin door. "Weapons stay on the jetty, if you'd be so kind. Dessa will mind them."

A broad woman with a tarred braid takes your dagger with two fingers and does not smile. Past the door the cabin is warm and close, with a lamp swinging from a beam, charts nailed to the wall and a kettle ticking on a brazier. The canvas satchel you wore into the yard sits open on the table beside a plate of ship's biscuit. Ashgrove sits across from it, pours two cups of something that smells of mint, and slides one over.

"I should say at once that I'm not a cruel woman," she says. "You were a nuisance, not an enemy. Half the words I need are in your head and half in your Sister's. I'd rather have them given than taken." She turns her white glove over on the table. "You have a gift for being underestimated, Miss Thorne. I'd put it to better use than picking pockets on a river. A seat at my table, a share of the tribute, and Marrowmere kept dry. Nobody writing your script but you."

She knows your ideal. Outside the thin cabin walls, Corvin's chorus is closer now, and a boot scuffs on the deck above. Two guards stand inside the door and one at your back. Ysolt is still out in the reeds, waiting on your signal.

One note from the DM: your sheet now shows you carrying a brass lantern key and no rapier, so I'm following the sheet. You are at 13 of 15 hit points with no spell slots left.

entries.text:
Your hands stay raised and your tail stays tucked. You step onto the barrels as if the jetty were a stage and nobody has told you the play was cancelled. The sentry's crossbow tracks you the whole way, and a second man takes your skiff's line and makes it fast without being asked. Neither of them touches you.

Ashgrove inclines her head, almost approving. "Bring the cup, by all means. Dessa, her belt knives only, please. Let her keep her manners." A raider relieves you of your dagger with the care of a man handling a hornet's nest. Your two quick fingers, held down by your hip, go unnoticed. Across the water, Ysolt's dark shape stays exactly where it was.

The cabin is warm and low-beamed, with a stove ticking, a chart table and a kettle on a hook. Your satchel sits open on the table beside a white glove, which Ashgrove has taken off. The hand beneath it is thin and ink-stained, and a shining black burn scar crosses the back of it. She pours two cups and pushes one across. Four raiders crowd the doorway behind you. The brass key lies on the chart, and she has not touched it for the last minute.

"I have half the words, Miss Thorne," she says, and for once she isn't smiling. "Not through lack of asking. The Sleeper can be woken by anyone who holds the key at the new moon, but it will not obey the one who wakes it unless the Keepers' words are spoken over the lamp. Without them it simply wakes, and eats what's nearest. That would be Marrowmere, and then me." She turns her cup. "So. I need the words. You need the key. Let's be civilized, and let's both be a little honest. Name your price."

A table, a kettle, a cup and the key a forearm's reach away. Four men are at your back, and the clock is running on both sides.

A note as DM: your sheet now shows things I don't have in my notes (a second level, extra slots, a "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin", a brass key already on you). I'm treating the sheet as the truth for numbers and gear, and I'll keep the key on the table in the story until you tell me how it came to be on your sheet.

Ashgrove laughs, a short real laugh, and waves the sentry's crossbow down an inch. "Bring your cup, by all means. I like a guest with her own crockery." Her eyes follow your hand where it drifted to your hip and back, and she smiles a little at it. "And tell your friend on the far bank she may keep her bolt. If she shoots, my men shoot you, and we both lose the conversation."

The sentry with the scarred brow takes your dagger, politely and without fuss, and walks you up the plank with the crossbow a hand's breadth from your spine. The deck is slick with river-damp. There are more men than you counted from the skiff, six or seven, all in boiled leather and all watching you. Some are bandaged from the shrine yard.

The cabin is a toll-keeper's old counting-room, with a brazier, a kettle on a hook and a table nailed to the floor. Your satchel sits open on it, and beside it lies a brass lantern key, polished and warm in the brazier-light. Ashgrove sits down across the table, strips off her white glove at last, and lays it by the kettle. Her bare hand is scarred and mottled, as if it had once been badly burned.

"I'll be plain, Miss Thorne, since you were plain with the town. I have the key and the new moon. You and Sister Odalie have the words. I would rather pay for them than take them. A chair, a cup, and a share of what comes after." She pours two cups. "Marrowmere would have a patron instead of a graveyard. I'd even keep your shrine standing."

Outside, upriver, Corvin's off-key chorus carries across the water. The sentry has shut the cabin door behind you and stands with his back to it.

line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

She keeps her tail tucked and her eyes on the cabin door while she signals Ysolt with two slow fingers down by her hip: *wait.* "Mind if I bring my own cup? I'd like to hear what a woman with half the words offers for the other half."

entries.text: time: no timer named "Vesper's Disguise Self"; timers: none

Ashgrove's smile widens, and for the first time it looks nearly genuine. "A guest who brings her own cup. How refreshing." She steps aside from the cabin door with a small, gracious sweep of the white glove. "Do come in. Dessa, the crossbow may stay up. It's only polite to remember what we are to each other."

The sentry's bolt tracks you as you climb onto the barrels and up the gangplank, close enough that you feel it between your shoulder blades. On the deck the other two raiders fall in behind you. No one touches you, and no one searches you. It's the discipline of a captain who believes she holds every card.

Your signal goes unanswered from the reeds, as it should. Ysolt is a patient woman, and a fast one when she has to be.

Inside, the cabin is a surprise: a scrubbed table, a lamp, two stools, a steaming kettle on a little iron stove, and tidy maps weighted with teacups. Your satchel sits on the table beside a plate of ship's biscuit, its flap buckled. Ashgrove pours two cups with a steady hand and sits, and the door closes behind you on the singing from upriver.

"Now," she says, folding her gloved hand over her bare one. "You have half the words. I have the key, the barges and the night. Tell me what you want for the other half, Miss Thorne. I assure you, everyone has a price. It would be a shame to learn yours the hard way."

Three raiders stand behind you, and the lamp is bright. Your cup steams in front of you. What does Vesper do?

And the sheet lists half of a sluice-pin that belongs to Garrow Quill, the Weeping Locks' keeper, whom Ashgrove has bought. You palmed it off her map-table with the key, a split iron pin that opens the flood-gates only when both halves are drawn together. Quill has the other half. Without both, the gates could only be forced.

The *Plump Heron* poles upriver through the grey end of the night, past dark reed-beds and sleeping herons, and Corvin keeps a wary eye behind. Odalie is waiting on the bottom step in her grey habit with a lantern gone pale in the dawn, and she lets out a breath when she sees you. Behind her stand Brannoc Vell and Ysolt Pike, each with a cup of something steaming.

You have a key, half a pin, eight days minus one, and a flood to stop at the Weeping Locks. You are at 13 of 15 hit points with no spell slots until you rest.

Level up! New spell: Healing Word, since I've nearly died once already and a heal at range beats a prayer. No swaps, and I'll take the fixed 6 hit points, because I don't trust my luck with a d8 after that natural 1 at the hulk.

Then she holds up the key to the lantern light. "Corvin, drop us at Tanner's Stair by dawn. Ashgrove means to open the Weeping Locks at the new moon and drown the lower town, so I need Odalie, the Reeve, and a way to break that lock before then."

Nothing needs sending. Your sheet already shows you at level 2: 15 hit points, a third slot and Healing Word known. The next level is at 900 XP, and you have 425. When it comes you'll get Lore College, expertise in two skills and three bonus proficiencies, so think about those.

Two other things on the sheet:

- Your rapier is gone. You left it on a barrel at the hulk's jetty and the sentry took it. You still have the dagger. Getting a blade is worth thinking about.
- You hold "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin". I hadn't named it in play, so here's the ruling: Garrow Quill is the lock-keeper of the Weeping Locks. A two-part iron pin holds the flood-gates shut, and this was his half, tucked in the key's wrapping in the satchel. Without both halves the gates can't be opened on the new moon, so Ashgrove needs it, and Quill's fate is unknown.

The *Plump Heron* drifts through the grey hours, and Corvin sleeps at the tiller and Piet takes the poles. At dawn on Day 4 you reach Tanner's Stair, damp and aching but whole. Mags's door opens before you knock, and Odalie hurries out and holds you hard enough to hurt. Then she sees the key in your hand and her face goes still. "Both," she says. "She's taken the whole plan out of your pocket, hasn't she?"

You tell her about the Locks. She says nothing for a long moment, then turns and calls over her shoulder, "Brannoc. Bring the river chart again."

Six nights remain to the new moon. You have the key, half a pin, and a family. What does Vesper do?
